title: Iran says peace talks would be ’unreasonable’ following Israeli strikes
byline: Israel pounded Lebanon with its heaviest strikes yet on Wednesday, killing hundreds of people and drawing a threat of retaliation from Iran, which suggested it would be ’’unreasonable’’ to ‌proceed with talks to forge a permanent peace deal with the United States.

title: 14 passengers in one trishaw : driver arrested
byline: A trishaw driver was arrested by Koslanda Police yesterday for transporting 14 passengers, including schoolchildren and adults, in violation of the vehicle’s permitted seating capacity.

title: Trump warns U.S. military will stay near Iran until ‘real agreement’ is honored
byline: President Donald Trump said Wednesday U.S. military forces will remain deployed in and around Iran until Tehran fully complies with the “real agreement,” warning that any breach would trigger a military response larger than anything seen before.

title: Sri Lanka explores trade, security ties at Montana Summit
byline: A Sri Lankan delegation led by Ambassador Mahinda Samarasinghe participated in the Montana Security and Economic Summit - 2026, engaging in wide-ranging discussions with U.S. counterparts on trade, investment, education and security cooperation.

title: Israel reopens Jerusalem holy sites
byline: Israeli authorities have announced that major holy sites in Jerusalem will reopen to visitors and worshippers following a temporary ceasefire in the Middle East conflict.

title: Iran threatens new hostilities as Israel pounds Lebanon
byline: Hezbollah said on Thursday that it fired rockets at Israel in response to continued attacks despite the US-Iran ceasefire.

title: Contract to procure coal signed without AG’s approval
byline: A contract to procure coal was signed with Trident Chemphar Limited without obtaining the approval of the Attorney General, according to a report by the Auditor General investigating the alleged fraud.

title: JD Vance says Iran would be ‘dumb’ to let talks collapse over Lebanon
byline: United States Vice President JD Vance has warned Iran that it would be “dumb” to jeopardise its ceasefire with Washington over Israel’s attacks in Lebanon.

title: Iran’s IRGC navy issues map to guide ships around Hormuz mines
byline: Iran announced alternative routes on Thursday for ships traveling through the Strait of Hormuz, citing the risk of sea mines in the main zone of the vital waterway.

title: Sun overhead parts of country at 12:12 noon today
byline: The sun will be directly overhead parts of the country today (09) at approximately 12:12 noon, with the closest areas identified as Chilaw, Bingiriya, Halmillawewa, Panduwasnuwara, Gokarella, Kawudupelella, Koppaveli and Kirankulam.

title: Water supply cut announced for Homagama and surrounding areas
byline: Water supply to areas including Homagama town, Wekanda Road, Pinketha Road, Walawwa Road, Gemunu Mawatha, Athurugiriya Road, Galawilawatta, Niyandagala, Mahakatuwana, Magammana, Deniya and the Diyagama University area will be suspended from 8:00 p.m. today (9) to 8:00 a.m. on Friday, April 10, the National Water Supply and Dranage Board (NWSDB) said.

title: Sri Lanka Cricket to file objections against Nuwan Thushara’s petition
byline: Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) informed the Colombo District Court that it will file objections to the petition submitted by cricketer Nuwan Thushara, seeking an interim injunction compelling the the authorities to issue him a “No Objection Certificate” to enable his participation in the 2026 Indian Premier League and other international premier league tournaments.

title: Pakistan declares two-day holiday as US, Iran head to Islamabad for talks
byline: An Iranian delegation is set to arrive in Islamabad on Thursday night ahead of talks with the United States, Iran’s ambassador to Pakistan, Reza Amiri Moghadam, said. The visit comes amid ongoing diplomatic efforts to ease tensions in the Middle East following weeks of conflict.

title: Unacceptable behaviour by GMOA: Minister
byline: The behaviour of the Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA), which has launched a strike, is unacceptable, Minister of Health Nalinda Jayatissa told Parliament today.

title: This is how Colombo Fort Railway Station will look in 15 months: Minister
byline: Transport Minister Bimal Ratnayake has announced that the Colombo Fort Railway Station will be renovated and completed within 15 months, revealing a vision of how the station is expected to look after the project.

title: Doctors’ union urges CID probe into Lakvijaya coal deal
byline: The Doctors’ Trade Union Alliance for Medical and Civil Rights has formally requested the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to launch an immediate criminal investigation into the alleged procurement of undersized coal for the Lakvijaya Power Plant.

title: NDB manager among several arrested over internal fraud
byline: Police have arrested several individuals, including a manager of the National Development Bank (NDB), in connection with an internal financial fraud at the institution.

title: Nepal issues arrest warrant for former PM Deuba in graft probe
byline: Nepal has issued an arrest warrant for former Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba for alleged corruption, officials said on Thursday (April 9, 2026) , making him the latest high-profile figure targeted under the new government.

title: Sri Lanka reaches IMF staff-level agreement, $700M financing expected
byline: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and authorities of Sri Lanka have reached a staff-level agreement on economic policies to conclude the combined Fifth and Sixth Reviews under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF).

title: Sudden downpour in Pallekele causes several trees to fall
byline: A sudden heavy downpour accompanied by strong winds struck the Balagolla area in the Pallekele Police Division, causing several trees to fall.

title: Sri Lankan Ambassador meets Nepal new Prime Minister
byline: The Ambassador of Sri Lanka to Nepal, Ruwanthi Delpitiya, paid a joint courtesy call on Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah, together with Heads of Diplomatic Missions based in Kathmandu.

title: Former SL envoy to Iran hails Cardinal for taking on Donald Trump
byline: Former Sri Lankan Ambassador to Iran M. M. Zuhair said that Sri Lankans must honour Colombo Archbishop Cardinal Malcolm Ranjith for ‘hitting the nail right on its head’ over the Israeli-American war on Iran.

title: Maussakele and Castlereagh reservoirs down
byline: The capacity of the Maussakele and Castlereagh hydro power reservoirs are fast dwindling due to the prevailing dry weather experienced in the central hills.

title: Govt moves to revamp fuel, electricity pricing formulas
byline: A controversial move is underway to introduce a new formulas for adjusting fuel and electricity bills in the country, raising questions over its impact on already strained households.

title: Heat to ease with afternoon rains
byline: Amid sweltering daytime conditions, the Meteorology Department has warned of afternoon thundershowers across several parts of the island, with the public urged to remain vigilant over lightning and gusty winds.

title: NASA Artemis II astronauts prepare to end moon mission in ’fireball’ re-entry
byline: Four astronauts traveling back to Earth from the far side of the moon on NASA’s Artemis II mission spoke of their emotions as they wrapped up ​the unprecedented flight and prepared to re-enter the atmosphere in a ’’fireball’’, during their first press conference from space on Wednesday.

title: Tesla is developing a new smaller, cheaper EV, sources say.
byline: Tesla  is developing an all-new smaller, cheaper electric SUV, four people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

title: Oil prices rise as concerns grow over ’fragile’ US-Iran ceasefire
byline: Global oil prices have risen as concerns grow over whether a fragile US-Iran ceasefire will hold after Israel launched a wave of strikes on Lebanon.

title: Public urged to brace for rising heat as amber advisory issued
byline: Residents across multiple provinces have been alerted to expect heightened heat conditions following an Amber-level warm weather advisory issued by the Natural Hazards Early Warning Centre at 3:30 p.m. today (9).

title: Illegal quartz mining site in Wellawaya raided; Equipment and minerals seized
byline: An unauthorized quartz mining operation in the Kotikambokka area of Alikota Ara in Wellawaya was raided by officers of the Sri Lanka Police Special Task Force in collaboration with the Geological Survey and Mines Bureau (GSMB), officials said.

title: Israel launches fresh strikes on Lebanon after huge attacks jeopardise truce
byline: Israel bombed more targets in Lebanon on Thursday, putting the Middle ​East ceasefire in further jeopardy after its biggest attacks of the war on its neighbour killed more than 250 people and threatened to torpedo Donald Trump’s truce from the outset.

title: Iran war doubles Russia’s main oil revenue to $9 bln in April: Reuters
byline: Russia will see revenue from its biggest ‌single oil tax double to $9 billion in April due to the oil and gas crisis triggered by the U.S. and Israeli attack on Iran, Reuters calculations showed on Thursday.

title: Education Ministry warns against high-cost school events
byline: The Education Ministry has issued a directive urging schools to exercise financial prudence when organizing festivals and other celebrations, following concerns over excessive spending that may place an additional burden on parents.

title: Fundamental rights petition seeks levy on single-use polythene bags
byline: A Fundamental Rights petition has been filed in the Supreme Court seeking the immediate introduction of a regulated levy on single-use polythene bags, along with a structured mechanism to promote environmentally friendly alternatives.

title: Sri Lankan-origin student elected to French City Council at 18
byline: A French student of Sri Lankan origin, Bilaal Lookman, has been elected as a municipal councillor in his hometown of Guyancourt, on the outskirts of Paris, at just 18 years old, making him one of the youngest elected officials in France.

title: QR-based tea fertilizer system surpasses 2024/25 in 6 months
byline: The distribution of subsidized tea fertilizer through Sri Lanka’s new QR-based system has shown significant progress within six months since its launch on October 1, surpassing performance recorded in the 2024/2025 period.

title: Specialist doctors not supporting GMOA strike: AMS
byline: The Association of Medical Specialists (AMS) said the specialist doctors will not join the 48-hour island-wide strike, which was launched by the Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA).

title: Parliament approves extension of emergency
byline: Parliament approved the resolution to extend the emergency by a majority of 110 votes with 137 members voting in favour and 27 against.

title: Spain condemns Israeli attacks on Lebanon, reopens Tehran embassy
byline: Spain’s Foreign Minister Jose Manuel ​Albares on Thursday accused Israel of violating ‌international law and a newly brokered two-week ceasefire in the Middle East by carrying out airstrikes ​on Lebanon on Wednesday.

title: IMF stresses need for trade liberalisation, digitisation, regulatory streamlining to unlock growth in Sri Lanka
byline: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) stressed today that Sri Lanka must also continue with trade liberalisation, digitalisation, regulatory streamlining, and labour market modernisation to unlock durable, inclusive growth.

title: 10–15 forest fires reported this year due to hot weather: DMC
byline: At least 10 to 15 forest fire incidents have been reported so far this year due to the prevailing hot weather conditions, Director of the Disaster Management Centre, Pradeep Kodippili said.

title: Speaker, Parliament Secretariat mum on opposition MPs using unparliamentary language: Bimal
byline: Leader of the House Bimal Rathnayake today made a serious accusation against the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker and the Parliament Secretariat for not taking action against Opposition MPs who use unparliamentary language in the House, specially targeting female MPs of the ruling party.

title: Heat to intensify after June: Meteorology official
byline: Heat conditions in the country are likely to intensify in the months following June, Additional Director General of the Department of Meteorology, Ajith Wijemanne said.

title: Colombo Fort Railway Station modernization project launched
byline: The government officially commenced the modernization of the Colombo Fort Railway Station today, (April 9). The project’s inauguration was presided over by Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya at the station premises.

title: Water cut announced for Homagama and surrounding areas
byline: Water supply to areas including Homagama town, Wekanda Road, Pinketha Road, Walawwa Road, Gemunu Mawatha, Athurugiriya Road, Galawilawatta, Niyandagala, Mahakatuwana, Magammana, Deniya and the Diyagama University area will be suspended from 8:00 p.m. today (9) to 8:00 a.m. on Friday, April 10, the National Water Supply and Dranage Board (NWSDB) said.

title: Brazil’s Laura Cardoso makes T20I history with nine-wicket haul
byline: Laura Cardoso etched her name into the record books, becoming the first player in either men’s or women’s T20I cricket to pick up nine wickets in a single innings.

title: New Year kevili table cost increases by 7% from 2025 to 2026
byline: The cost of ingredients required to prepare a traditional “kevili” table for the Sinhala and Tamil New Year has increased by 7.0% in 2026 compared to 2025, and by 2.5 times compared to 2019—prior to the pandemic and economic crisis.

title: Lebanon PM asks Pakistan to confirm country’s inclusion in truce talks
byline: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam has asked his Pakistani counterpart to confirm Lebanon’s inclusion in the Iran war ceasefire, a day after Israeli strikes on the country killed more than 200 people.

title: Excise seizes Rs.20Mn worth imported booze kept for Avurudu
byline: A large stock of imported foreign liquor worth over Rs.20 million, kept ready for distribution during the Avurudu season, was seized by the Department of Excise from a location in Wellawatta this week.

title: Islamabad locks down for first US-Iran talks as Israeli attacks on Lebanon jeopardise truce
byline: Israel bombed more targets in Lebanon on Thursday, putting the U.S.-Iran ​ceasefire into further jeopardy after the biggest Israeli attacks on its neighbour of the war killed more than 250 people and threatened to torpedo Donald Trump’s truce.

title: Market slides amid early selling pressure, partial recovery fails to lift indices
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange witnessed a subdued and cautious trading session on 09th March 2026, as early selling pressure weighed heavily on market performance despite a modest recovery later in the day. The ASPI declined sharply during the first hour of trading, reflecting weak investor sentiment at the open.

title: Government to modernize public transport for safety and convenience
byline: The government’s objective is to transform public transportation into a safe, technologically advanced service that can be used with convenience by all citizens.

title: CAA launches action against overpricing in trains and canteens
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has launched strict legal action against traders engaging in overpricing and failing to display price information in trains and railway station canteens.

title: Record lottery prize to be awarded tomorrow
byline: The Ministry of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Co-operative Development is preparing to award the largest lottery prize in its history, with a winning cheque exceeding Rs. 620 million.

title: FSP challenges legality of coal tenders, plans court action
byline: The Frontline Socialist Party (FSP) has raised serious allegations over the awarding of two coal tenders, claiming that both long-term and emergency contracts are illegal and calling for legal intervention.

title: PHI conduct surprise inspections in Nuwara Eliya ahead of spring festival
byline: Public Health Inspectors (PHI) conducted surprise inspections across Nuwara Eliya town on April 9, targeting restaurants, bakeries, and wholesale and retail shops ahead of the upcoming Spring Festival, in a bid to ensure quality and safety for consumers.

title: NASA Artemis II astronauts prepare to end moon mission in ’fireball’ re-entry
byline: Four astronauts traveling back to Earth from the far side of the moon on NASA’s Artemis II mission spoke of their emotions as they wrapped up ​the unprecedented flight and prepared to re-enter the atmosphere in a ’’fireball’’, during their first press conference from space on Wednesday.

title: Special trains announced for New Year travel
byline: Sri Lanka Railways Department (SLRD) has announced the operation of several special trains to facilitate passenger travel during the upcoming Sinhala and Tamil New Year period.

title: Head of IMF says Iran war will permanently scar global economy even if peace is reached
byline: The head of the International Monetary Fund has warned that the Iran war will permanently scar the global economy even if a durable peace deal in the Middle East can be reached.

title: Houthi leader hails US-Iran truce as ‘major victory’ for Tehran
byline: The leader of Yemen’s Houthis, Abdel-Malik al-Houthi, has described the recently agreed ceasefire between the US and Iran as a “great victory” for Tehran and the so-called “axis of resistance”, a network of Iran-aligned groups across the Middle East.

title: US plans to automatically register men for military draft eligibility
byline: Young American men could be automatically registered for eligibility for the military draft as soon as December, ending decades of self-registration.

title: Hormuz at near standstill as Iran warns ships to keep to its waters
byline: Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz stood at well below 10% of normal volumes on Thursday ​despite a U.S.-Iran ceasefire as Tehran asserted its control by warning ships to keep to its territorial waters while doing so.Hundreds of tankers ‌and other ships have been stuck inside the Gulf since the Iran war began on Feb 28, cutting global oil supply by 20% in the world’s biggest-ever supply disruption.

title: Electric wheelchairs donated to war-disabled veterans
byline: A special programme to donate modern electric wheelchairs to war-disabled veterans was held today at the Ranaviru Seva Authority (RSA) office.
